Title
 Standard Practices for 
 Preparation of Metallographic Specimen
Procedure

Metallographic 
 Practice Generally Applicable to all Metals. Using Hand Book ( Volume 8 )1975
Introduction

According to the directives of the Central Chemical Laboratories this practice 
covers the preparation of Metallographic Specimen for failure analysis.

This branch of metallography is variously called light metallography, 
visible-light metallography, or optical metallography, to distinguish it from 
electron metallography.
Significance

Examination of defects that appear in finished or partly finished product and 
studies of parts that have failed in service.

Summary of 
Practice
Preparation of Metallographic Specimen generally requires five major operations:
Sectioning,
Mounting,
Grinding,
Polishing and
Etching.

Etching.

sections.text: Sampling
A well-prepared Metallographic Specimen is:
A representative sample,

Sectioned, ground and polished so as to minimize disturbed or flowed surince 
 metal caused by mechanical deformation, and thus to allow the true 
 microstructure to be revealed by etching,
Free from polishing scratches and pits and liquid staining,
Polished so that inclusions are preserved intact,
Flat enough to permit examination at high magnification.

sections.text: Safety Precautions

items:
Solvents such as HF, HCL, HNO3, and 
H2SO4 acids are dangerous, they 
will expose lung to very hazardous so you have to wear breathing mask.

Keep these solvents closed and in a hood. Do not get them in the 
eyes, on the skin, or on clothing.

Using of bacalite is very dangerous and 
carcinogenic chemical, so you must not breath the vapor of it, and keep 
it away from skin by using gloves.

sections.text:
Tools and 
Equipment

Cut off Machine- 
Provides safety, convenience and routinely produces high quality surface 
finishes with minimal deformation. The cut off machine operates in either manual 
or automatic mode and provided with coolant pumb.

Mounting Press Equipment- 
The mold produced is cylindrical in shape with 1.25 in from bacalite material 
under heat and pressure.

Grind Equipment- 
Using abrasive grit and grit size from 60 mesh through 600 mesh.

Polisher Equipment- 
By using of cloth-covered laps (velvet) and suitable polishing abrasives as ( 
Alumina ).
Work to be Carried out
Specimen Preparation

Cut the metal 
specimen by a high-speed cutter into a small piece. Then, in order to prevent 
specimen from change of structure because of frictional temperature, cool down 
the specimen by soapy water or water itself as well as light oil.

By using a 
file, flat the specimen.

Make the 
rough polishing as follows.

Polish the 
specimen by using the emery paper No. 60.

Move the 
specimen on the emery papers in one-way direction. Polish the specimen until the 
scratch made by emery paper disappear from the specimen surface.

When the 
emery paper is changed to another type, wash the specimen by water.

Nextly, use 
emery papers 120, 240, 320, 400, 600 in order, without omitting any of them.

sections.text: 4. Make the final polishing as follows.

Permeate 
the polishing cloth by dripped water. Gradually drop a suitable volume of 
polishing fluid from the plastic bottle while the specimen is equally pressed.

Slowly run 
the specimen between from edge to center of the disc while the disc rotates. 
Slowly move the specimen in reversed direction against rotation of disc in order 
to prevent from COMET-TAIL. Final polishing is allowed with low speed by placing 
the specimen at 25-50 mm distant from the center of the disc for 3-5 minutes.
